# cargo-project-tools

> A cargo subcommand that installs a project's cargo tools from Cargo.lock files kept in the project's own repository, so you can audit them and bump vulnerable dependencies without waiting for a tool release.

Source: https://github.com/osseco/cargo-project-tools

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://osseco.github.io/cargo-project-tools/docs/getting-started.md): install, verify, add, audit and install a first tool
- [How it works](https://osseco.github.io/cargo-project-tools/docs/how-it-works.md): why own locks, the .project-tools layout, what to commit
- [Commands](https://osseco.github.io/cargo-project-tools/docs/commands.md): every command and option
- [Configuration](https://osseco.github.io/cargo-project-tools/docs/configuration.md): project-tools.toml, audit-ignore.toml, sfw
- [Build review](https://osseco.github.io/cargo-project-tools/docs/build-review.md): approving, overriding or stripping build scripts, proc macros and shipped cargo config
- [CI](https://osseco.github.io/cargo-project-tools/docs/ci.md): GitHub Actions caching and auditing
- [AI agents](https://osseco.github.io/cargo-project-tools/docs/agents.md): how an agent chooses features with inspect, prepares the build review from JSON records, and what it must leave to the person
- [Verifying a release](https://osseco.github.io/cargo-project-tools/docs/verifying-releases.md): attestations, cosign, checksums
